newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FOCUS - Taiwan stocks seesaw at 10,000 threshold.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Taiwan stocks seesaw at 10,000 threshold.

text.p: Taiwan's red hot stock index on Tuesday sliced through psychological resistance at 10,000 points in intraday trade, but failed to maintain the momentum as late profit-taking erased the early gains, brokers said.

Brokers nevertheless said a new push above 10,000 was likely and consensus was growing that the index could touch 12,000 in the near term given Taiwan's economic fundamentals -- especially in the trendsetting electronics sector.
The benchmark index surged to an intraday peak of 10,057.95 in early trade, but lost steam in late trade to end at 9,892.34, down 30.71 points or 0.31 percent from Monday's close.
Investors uncorked champagne when the index first breached 10,000, but their ecstasy was short-lived as the market-leading electronics began to fade, then turn sharply lower.
Profit-taking against high-priced electronics shares was conspicuous, sinking the technology index by 2.73 percent.

Microchip blue chip Taiwan Semiconductor, whose fortunes guide the sector, sank steadily on word that Dutch giant Philips Electronic NV was selling 100 million of its shares. Taiwan Semicon closed T$10 lower at T$146.
United Microelectronics, echoing its rival's downturn, lost T$5.5 at T$134.
Acer Sertek, an arm of computer giant Acer Inc, dipped T$7 to T$104. Acer itself rose in early trade but had lost T$0.5 to T$98 by the close.
"Had electronics soared, the overall stock index should have been able to stand above 10,000," said Alex Yang of National Securities.
Brokers said heavy psychological pressure at five-digit levels simply wore down investors' confidence.
"If investors can overcome this pressure, it won't be a question for the index to push past 10,000 points tomorrow (Wednesday)," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.

Prominent market watchers said Taiwan's economy was healthy enough to justify a rise above 12,000 -- and even a test of the all-time high 12,495.34 -- and that electronics' downside would be short-lived.

"I think it (a test of the record) is very likely, given the strong performance of the electronics industry...and their optimistic earnings projections," Morris Li, vice president and country treasurer at Citibank Taiwan, told Reuters Financial Television.

Taiwan's economy broke out of a 1995-6 slump by posting strong 6.83 percent gross domestic product growth in the first quarter. The government forecasts full-year GDP growth at 6.24 percent -- far exceeding the 5.71 percent of 1996.

High-tech shares have been the driving force behind a rough doubling of the main index in the 16 months since rival China's military menacing of Taiwan sent stock market funds fleeing into foreign exchange, gold and other safe havens.
The sector rose a whopping 111 percent in the first half of 1997 and is widely tipped to enjoy sizzling second half sales.
